description: Conformal welding decomposes a Jordan curve into a pair of conformal maps. For the extremal Bloch domain, the welding homeomorphism encodes the boundary geometry. The 'conformal bootstrap' — imposing consistency conditions on welding data — can narrow the space of possible extremal domains, producing tighter bounds on B_u.
mathematical_formalization: Welding homeomorphism h: S^1 → S^1 satisfies f_+ = f_- ∘ h. For Bloch extremals: f_- univalent with f_-'(0)=1, f_+(D*) contains no disk > B_u, ||μ_h||_∞ < 1. Bootstrap: positivity of functionals of h bounds B_u.
implementation_hypothesis: Represent h as Fourier series. Impose covering radius = R and derive positivity constraints. Solve resulting SDP feasibility problem. Binary search on R.
experiment_seed: For N=10 Fourier modes, set up feasibility SDP. Binary search: largest infeasible R gives upper bound.
